what: On the one full Windows run on FFmpeg 9.1.0 two tests failed with nothing wrong in a tool: test_multicam_switch_energy_picks_the_loudest_camera gave 10.25-12 s to camera 0, and test_loudness_keeps_each_sound_where_its_picture_is ran its -30 LUFS target in loudnorm's dynamic mode, so the two targets no longer covered both modes. The multicam pair shared no sound (a 440 Hz tone each, loud and quiet swapped): the alignment put camera 1 6.017 s late on 6.1.1 too, and every late window was a tie between two tones at 0.01 that the encoder's noise decided. The loudness fixture's four equal beeps measured a range of 0.10 LU, next to loudnorm's rule that a range of 0 is dynamic at any target. A third waited for the next 9.1 run: test_waveform_without_image_is_byte_identical_to_1_15 pins waveform.py's whole argv with `-c:a aac -b:a 192k`, and from 9.1 the runner writes `-aac_coder twoloop` between them (#660), so it fails there with nothing wrong (found with the pin forced on, on 6.1.1).
escaped: Both tests asserted the outcome (the picks, the set of modes) and not the condition it rested on (an alignment of 0 s, a range clear of 0), and every build CI ran before 9.1 happened to land on the passing side; the CI pin to 9.0.2 then hid the failures while #660 fixed the coder.
mechanism: Each test now asserts its fixture's condition before the outcome, and fails on the old fixture on every build: the multicam test asserts camera 1's offset is 0 s (the old pair measures 6.017 s on 6.1.1), the loudness test asserts each gapped fixture's range is at least 1 LU (the old one measures 0.10) and prints each run's mode, range and ceiling when the modes check fails. ci.yml installs 9.1.0 on Windows, so the whole suite runs on the version that showed it. The waveform test applies runner.pin_aac_coder to its expected argv, as it applies bt709_tag_args(), so it follows the build it runs on.
